title: fix(audio): route extracted audio paths to AudioSourceConfig.file (#4395)
body:
## Problem

Crashlytics issue `e81e2bc1d6713fa5d91e7b15a0950e18` (16 events, 2 users, v1.0.13):

```txt
StateError: Bad state: No host specified in URI ...extracted_audio_xxx.wav
  _HttpClient.getUrl
  AudioClipPlayer._defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader
  AudioClipPlayer.setClip
  AudioTimingCubit._setClippedAudioSource
```

`AudioEvent.url` is overloaded: it contains either network URLs **or** bare absolute file paths (e.g. from `clip_editor_bloc.dart` via `extractAudio(videoPath)`). `AudioTimingCubit` classified everything non-bundled as `.network`; the default remote loader passed the path without scheme validation to `HttpClient.getUrl`.

## Fix

- **`AudioTimingCubit`** (primary): three-way classification in `_setClippedAudioSource`
  - bundled → `AudioSourceConfig.asset`
  - `file://` URI or bare absolute path (starts with `/`) → `AudioSourceConfig.file` (decoded via `Uri.toFilePath()`)
  - otherwise → `AudioSourceConfig.network`

- **`AudioClipPlayer`** (defense-in-depth): `_defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader` now throws `ArgumentError` for non-http(s) schemes instead of silently passing a broken URI to `HttpClient.getUrl`.



Closes #4395

body:
## Summary

First sub-batch (9a of 3) of #4506's final wave. Refs #4339 Wave 2.

Moves the 10-entity upload/media cluster to `lib/providers/upload_media_providers.dart`. **Cleanest cluster of the entire wave** — pure dependency injection, no in-line state machines, no bridges, no follow-up smells.

## What moved

**Private adapters** (preserved through batches 5/7 and now moving with their callers):
- `_BlossomAuthAdapter` — implements `BlossomAuthProvider`
- `_FirebasePerformanceAdapter` — implements `BlossomPerformanceMonitor`

**Media auth chain:**
- `blossomAuthService`
- `mediaViewerAuthServiceProvider` (legacy `Provider<X>(...)` style)
- `mediaAuthInterceptor`

**Upload chain:**
- `blossomUploadService`
- `uploadManager` (top of upload chain)

**API + audio:**
- `apiService` (nip98-backed)
- `crosspostApiClient` (Bluesky-toggle settings)
- `audioPlaybackService`

## Migration pattern

`app_providers.dart` adds:

\`\`\`dart
import 'package:openvine/providers/upload_media_providers.dart';  // back-import for bugReportService
// ...
export 'upload_media_providers.dart';  // keeps 28 consumers' imports unchanged
\`\`\`

- The **import** is needed because `bugReportService` (line 945, will move with batch 9c) still consumes `blossomUploadServiceProvider`.
- The **export** keeps all 28 external consumer files unchanged.

**No mutual import** — the new file does NOT import `app_providers.dart`. All outbound deps reach already-split files: `auth_providers.dart` (authService, oauthClient, oauthConfig, nip98AuthService), `moderation_providers.dart` (ageVerificationService, contentFilterService), `environment_provider.dart` (currentEnvironmentProvider). First batch of the wave with this shape.

## Discovered during implementation

`AudioPlaybackService` lives in the `sound_service` package, not at `openvine/services/audio_playback_service.dart` (a path I assumed in the plan and that doesn't exist). Corrected the import.

## Scope cleanup

`dart fix --apply` removed 9 newly-unused imports from `app_providers.dart` (blossom_upload_service, api_service, auth_service, crosspost_api_client, media_auth_interceptor, media_viewer_auth_service, performance_monitoring_service, upload_manager, audio_playback_service via sound_service).

Codegen moved: 6 `*Provider` chunks (~378 LoC) relocated from `app_providers.g.dart` into `upload_media_providers.g.dart`. Zero duplication (verified via grep).

## Summary

Follow-up cleanup from PR #4534 (batch 8 — video/feed providers split). Closes #4544.

Three `.initialize()` `.catchError` sites in `lib/providers/video_providers.dart` were moved verbatim from `app_providers.dart` and carry two pieces of post-move debt:

2. **Tag**: stale `name: 'AppProviders'` — these providers no longer live in `app_providers.dart`. title: feat(recorder/library): clip trash bin with 30-day retention
body:
Closes #4547

## Summary

Replaces the recorder's destructive "delete last clip" gesture with a
two-layer safety net:

1. **Snackbar Undo (5 s)** — taps to the bottom-left button now schedule a
   soft-delete and show a "Clip moved to trash • Undo" snackbar. Undo
   restores the clip to its original tray position.
2. **30-day trash bin** — clips that aren't undone land in a new
   *Recently deleted* screen (accessible from the clips library), where
   they sit for 30 days before auto-purge. Each row offers Restore /
   Delete now, plus a single "Empty trash" action.

Library-tab deletes are routed through the same `softDelete` path so
both surfaces share one delete behavior. Icon swapped from
`arrowCounterClockwise` → `trash` so the affordance reads as
*destructive-but-recoverable* instead of *undo my last tap*.

Motivation: in-app feedback from `723glimmers` — accidentally tapped
"undo" while assembling a brownie-batter compilation and lost a step.
The undo button's icon promised reversibility but the action was a
single-tap, no-confirm, on-disk hard delete with no recovery.

## Architecture

- **Schema:** `clips.deleted_at` (nullable timestamp) + idx_clip_deleted_at.
  All existing read paths now filter `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- **`ClipLibraryService`** split into `softDelete` / `restore` /
  `hardDelete` / `getTrashedClips` / `purgeExpiredTrash`. `softDelete`
  optionally clears `draft_id` so a recorder-trashed clip lands in the
  library on restore rather than a stale session.
- **`ClipManagerNotifier`** tracks the pending deletion in state, commits
  it on `addClip` / `reorderClip` / `clearAll` / dispose so a fresh
  recording never leaks a half-undone state.
- **`ClipsLibraryBloc`** gains four events: `TrashLoadRequested`,
  `RestoreClips`, `HardDeleteClip`, `EmptyTrash`, plus `trashedClips`
  and `lastDeletedClipIds` on state.
- **`purgeExpiredTrash(retention: 30d)`** runs on app startup from
  `app_lifecycle_handler.dart` (best-effort, idempotent).

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/services/clip_library_service_test.dart` — softDelete / restore / hardDelete / purgeExpiredTrash coverage
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/clips_library` — 64 tests, including state-prop shape after new fields
- [x] `flutter test test/providers/clip_manager_provider_test.dart` — `scheduleDeleteLastClip` smoke
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/video_recorder` — both recording modes
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/library test/screens/library_screen_test.dart` — library entry-point unchanged for existing flows
- [x] `flutter test test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` — new keys allowlisted
- [x] `packages/db_client` migration test — schema add safe
- [ ] Manual: capture-mode tap → snackbar → Undo → restored
- [ ] Manual: capture-mode tap → snackbar dismiss → clip in *Recently deleted* → Restore → library
- [ ] Manual: classic-mode same flow
- [ ] Manual: trash → Delete now → file gone
- [ ] Manual: trash → Empty trash → all files gone
- [ ] Manual: kill app, relaunch → trashed clips persisted

## l10n

Eight new keys: `videoRecorderClipUndoLabel` + 7 `libraryTrash*` keys.
Allowlisted in `arb_consistency_test.dart`; translators will pick them
up in the next localization pass. `videoRecorderClipDeletedMessage`
English copy updated from "Clip deleted" → "Clip moved to trash";
other locales fall back to the prior translation until refreshed.

title: refactor(logging): route raw print and debug logging through unified_logger

Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
Medium

## Problem
App and package code still uses print, debugPrint, and direct developer.log outside unified_logger, while analyzer allows it.

## Evidence
- mobile/analysis_options.yaml:56 disables avoid_print.
- mobile/lib/main.dart:585 calls print.
- mobile/lib/services/video_loading_metrics.dart:50, :56, :184, and :440 call print.
- mobile/lib/services/native_proofmode_service.dart:119 and :486 call print.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/rpc/keycast_rpc.dart:38, :50, and :55 call print.
- mobile/lib/scripts/migrate_logging.dart:72-103 documents intended migration patterns.
- mobile/packages/unified_logger/lib/src/unified_logger.dart:255 provides a Log.print wrapper.

## Impact
Logs bypass category filtering, capture, redaction conventions, and production verbosity controls. Some log sites include IDs, URLs, or operational details that should be centrally governed.

## Recommended fix
Migrate raw logging to Log.debug/info/warning/error with categories, then re-enable avoid_print with narrow exceptions for CLI scripts or examples.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No production app/package code calls raw print.
- [ ] debugPrint and direct developer.log are limited to unified_logger internals or documented exceptions.
- [ ] avoid_print is enabled.
- [ ] Logging tests or grep checks prevent regression.

title: refactor(providers): split video & feed providers out of app_providers.dart
body:
## Summary

Eighth batch of #4506 (app_providers.dart decomposition). Refs #4339 Wave 2.

Moves the 16-entity video/feed cluster to `lib/providers/video_providers.dart`. **Includes the most-consumed provider in the codebase** — `videoEventServiceProvider` has 80 external consumer files.

## What moved

**Leaves:** `videoFilterBuilder`, `videoVisibilityManager`, `seenVideosService`, `brokenVideoTracker`, `videoLocalStorage`, `personalEventCacheService`

**Keystone:** `subscriptionManager`, `videoEventService` (5 setter calls + OG Viner observer bridge)

**Publishers:** `videoEventPublisher`, `viewEventPublisher`, `subscribedListVideoCache`, `videoSharingService`, `videoMetadataUpdateService`

**Repositories:** `videosRepository`, `likesRepository`, `repostsRepository`

## What deliberately stays in `app_providers.dart`

`createBlockedAuthorFilter` (renamed from `_createBlockedAuthorFilter` to make it public) stays because two non-video providers still call it: `curatedListRepository` and `peopleListsRepository`. `videosRepository` in the new file calls it via the back-import. Same posture as `videoFilterBuilder` staying behind in batch 5.

## Migration pattern

`app_providers.dart` gets both:

\`\`\`dart
import 'package:openvine/providers/video_providers.dart';  // back-import
// ...
export 'video_providers.dart';  // keeps 107 consumers' imports unchanged
\`\`\`

- The **import** is non-optional — `analyticsService` (`viewEventPublisherProvider`), `hashtagService` (`videoEventServiceProvider`), `curationRepository` (`videoEventServiceProvider`, `likesRepositoryProvider`), and other internal app_providers callers still consume the moved symbols.
- The **export** keeps all 107 external consumer files unchanged.

Mutual import with `app_providers.dart`: the new file imports back for `databaseProvider`, `profileRepositoryProvider`, `funnelcakeApiClientProvider`, `pendingActionServiceProvider`, `uploadManagerProvider`, `blossomUploadServiceProvider`, `savedSoundsServiceProvider`, `ogVinerCacheServiceProvider`, `curatedListsStateProvider`, `dmRepositoryProvider`. Same shape as moderation/auth (batches 6/7).

## Scope cleanup

- `dart fix --apply` removed 20+ now-unused service/repository imports from `app_providers.dart` (services for moved providers + redundant transitive imports).
- Renamed `_createBlockedAuthorFilter` → `createBlockedAuthorFilter` to expose it across the back-import boundary.

Codegen moved: 16 `*Provider` chunks (~951 LoC) relocated from `app_providers.g.dart` into `video_providers.g.dart`.

## Out-of-scope follow-ups (rolled into existing lists)

1. **`videoEventService` setter pattern + observer bridge.** 5 `setX()` calls after construction + inline `addVideoObserver` lambda for OG Viner cache learning. Already tracked under #3334 (split VideoEventService into focused boundaries).
2. **`personalEventCacheService.initialize` + `likesRepository.initialize` log level.** `Log.error` for expected network/IO init failures; should be `Log.warning` per matrix.

## Test plan

- [x] `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — clean
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean (after `dart fix` removed 20+ unused imports)
- [x] `flutter test test/providers/video_events_provider_blocklist_test.dart test/providers/video_events_provider_buffering_test.dart test/providers/video_events_provider_list_stability_test.dart test/providers/video_events_provider_listener_test.dart test/widgets/video_feed_item/feed_videos_test.dart` — **28 passed**
- [x] `dart format` applied

After batches 1–8 (assuming all merge): `app_providers.dart` shrinks by ~1,800 LoC from the original 2,918 (~62% reduction). **One batch remains: Upload/Media + remainder** — the final sweep.

title: fix: audio progressively gets louder during iOS recording after using countdown feature
body:
## Summary
On iOS, the audio recorded during a video recording session gradually increases in volume over time. The issue appears to be triggered specifically when the countdown feature is used before starting the recording.

## Environment
- Platform: iOS
- Feature involved: Camera countdown

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open the camera screen
2. Enable / use the countdown feature to start a recording
3. Record a video with audio
4. Play back the recorded video

## Actual Result
The audio volume progressively increases throughout the recording — the longer the recording, the louder the audio becomes.

## Expected Result
Audio volume should remain consistent and stable throughout the entire recording session.

## Regression?
Appears to be related to the countdown feature — the issue does not occur (or is less noticeable) when recording is started without using the countdown.

## Evidence
Reported on Discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1470168817589158040/1470255950408454164/1504547798572466196)

body:

  Please look at the following checklist to ensure that your PR can be accepted quickly:

## Description
On cold start, VideoFeedBloc._onStarted unconditionally used .skip(1) on followingStream, dropping the first emission even when FollowRepository hadn't finished initialize() yet. If the Funnelcake /feed endpoint returned stale or popular-fallback content (because the server's follow-graph index wasn't ready), no corrective refresh ever fired and the Following feed showed the same content as For You.

Fix: capture isInitialized before subscribing and use .skip(0) when the repo was not yet initialized. The first post-initialize() emission then reaches _onFollowingListChanged, which performs a skipCache refresh with the real follow list.

When the repo was already initialized at startup time the existing .skip(1) behaviour is preserved to avoid a redundant second API call.

title: refactor(providers): split auth & identity providers out of app_providers.dart
body:
## Summary

Seventh batch of #4506 (app_providers.dart decomposition). Refs #4339 Wave 2.

Moves the 21-entity auth/identity cluster to mobile/lib/providers/auth_providers.dart. This is the largest cluster of the wave: authServiceProvider has 91+ external consumers and 33+ internal app_providers.dart references.

## What moved

Foundational stack: secureKeyStorage, flutterSecureStorage, secureKeycastStorage, oauthConfig, oauthClient, pendingVerificationService, passwordResetListener, emailVerificationListener, webAuthService, nostrKeyManager, plus the _productionLoginOrigin constant.

Keystone: authService, currentAuthState, currentAuthRpcCapability, knownAccounts.

Identity adjuncts: nostrCreatorBindingServiceProvider, cawgVerifierBaseUriProvider, cawgVerifierClientProvider, zendeskIdentitySync plus the _setZendeskIdentity helper, verifierClient, identityClaimsRepository, nip98AuthService, accountDeletionService.

## Deliberately not moved

Three media-adjacent auth providers stay in app_providers.dart because they are media-domain and will move with batch 9:
- blossomAuthService, along with the private _BlossomAuthAdapter class
- mediaViewerAuthServiceProvider
- mediaAuthInterceptor

## Migration pattern

app_providers.dart now both imports and re-exports auth_providers.dart so internal callers keep resolving locally while existing consumer imports remain unchanged.

Mutual import with app_providers.dart remains intentional: auth_providers reads profileRepositoryProvider for _setZendeskIdentity and userDataCleanupServiceProvider for the authService factory. This matches the moderation_providers to app_providers pattern from batch 6.

## Scope cleanup

Removed 17 now-unused imports from app_providers.dart via dart fix --apply.

Codegen moved: 15+ provider chunks moved from app_providers.g.dart into auth_providers.g.dart.

## Follow-up

- Remaining architectural debt is now tracked in #4533: extracting zendeskIdentitySync and _setZendeskIdentity coordination out of the provider layer.

## Test plan

Moves the entire 10-entity notifications cluster — 8 providers + 1 file-private helper + 1 `@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)` side-effect bridge — to a new `lib/providers/notifications_providers.dart`. Behavior preserved verbatim.

## What moved

|---|---|---|
| 1 | `firebaseMessagingProvider` | `Provider<FirebaseMessaging>` |
| 2 | `firebaseOnMessageProvider` | `Provider<Stream<RemoteMessage>>` |
| 3 | `notificationServiceProvider` | `Provider<NotificationService>` |
| 4 | `notificationPreferencesStoreProvider` | `Provider<NotificationPreferencesStore>` (Hive) |
| 5 | `pushNotificationServiceProvider` | `Provider<PushNotificationService?>` (gated on auth + session) |

| 8 | `notificationPreferencesServiceProvider` | `Provider<NotificationPreferencesService>` |
| 9 | `pushNotificationSync` | `@Riverpod(keepAlive: true) void` |
| 10 | `notificationServiceEnhanced` | `@riverpod NotificationServiceEnhanced` |

## Migration pattern

`app_providers.dart` adds `export 'notifications_providers.dart';`. No back-import — no remaining provider in `app_providers.dart` consumes any moved symbol. The collaborator block that was interleaved at lines 195-235 stays in `app_providers.dart` untouched.

The mutual `ref.read` between `notificationPreferencesServiceProvider` and `notificationPreferencesDirtySyncBridgeProvider` is preserved by co-locating them; the file-private `_updateNotificationPreferencesSafely` helper moves with them.

The new file imports `app_providers.dart` for `authServiceProvider`, `relayStatisticsServiceProvider`, `profileRepositoryProvider`, `videoEventServiceProvider`, and imports `database_provider.dart`, `environment_provider.dart`, `nostr_client_provider.dart` directly (these already-split files are reached without going through the `app_providers.dart` barrel).

## Scope cleanup

Removed seven now-unused imports from `app_providers.dart`: `firebase_messaging`, `flutter/foundation` (was only for `kIsWeb` in the moved `notificationServiceEnhanced`), `notification_preferences` (model), `notification_preferences_service`, `notification_service`, `push_notification_service`, `push_notification_session_coordinator`. Kept `notification_service_enhanced.dart` because `app_providers.dart` still calls `NotificationServiceEnhanced.instance.clearAllData()` from the sign-out cleanup callback.

Codegen moved: `pushNotificationSyncProvider` and `notificationServiceEnhancedProvider` chunks relocated from `app_providers.g.dart` into `notifications_providers.g.dart`.

## Out-of-scope findings to file as follow-ups

Two architectural smells surfaced during this investigation. I'm filing both as separate issues to keep this PR a pure relocation:

1. **Extract `NotificationPreferencesDirtySyncCoordinator` service.** The 95-line state machine inside the bridge provider (`activeDrainPubkeys`, `retryCountsByPubkey`, generation tokens, microtask scheduling) is repository/service-layer logic embedded in the providers layer. `architecture.md` says composition logic belongs in the repository.
2. **Resolve dead `notificationServiceEnhancedProvider`.** It has **zero `lib` consumers** — its `Future.microtask` / `Timer(3s)` init paths never execute in production. The singleton is initialized separately via `.instance` from `app_providers.dart:1303`. Per `state_management.md`, "BlocProvider is lazy by default" — same applies to Riverpod, and this provider is dead code unless someone reads it.

Both will be linked under #4339 Wave 4 once filed.

- [x] `flutter test test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart test/router/app_shell_notification_badge_test.dart test/screens/notification_settings_screen_test.dart` — **46 passed**

title: refactor(providers): split user-preference providers out of app_providers.dart
body:
## Summary

First batch of #4506 (app_providers.dart decomposition). Refs #4339 Wave 2.

Moves five user-preference providers out of `app_providers.dart` into a new `lib/providers/preferences_providers.dart`:
- `feedAspectRatioPreferenceServiceProvider`
- `audioSharingPreferenceService` (`@Riverpod`)
- `aiTrainingPreferenceService` (`@Riverpod`)
- `audioDevicePreferenceService` (`@Riverpod`)
- `languagePreferenceService` (`@Riverpod`)

## Migration pattern (validated in this PR)

`app_providers.dart` becomes a barrel that re-exports the new file:

\`\`\`dart
import 'package:openvine/providers/preferences_providers.dart';
// ...
export 'preferences_providers.dart';
\`\`\`

The `import` line is needed because two providers in `app_providers.dart` still consume `feedAspectRatioPreferenceServiceProvider` (`contentFilterVersion`, `videosRepository`). The `export` keeps the 295 existing consumer `import 'package:openvine/providers/app_providers.dart'` sites unchanged.

This pattern lets each batch land in <24h without rebase pain on consumer files, which is critical given `app_providers.dart` is the top merge hotspot (114 commits in 90 days).

## Scope

- Picked the preferences cluster as the validation batch because it's self-contained (only depends on `sharedPreferencesProvider`), has no bridge providers, and exercises both `Provider<X>(...)` and `@Riverpod`-annotated function styles.
- Removed five now-unused service imports from `app_providers.dart`.
- Regenerated codegen — moved chunks landed in the new `preferences_providers.g.dart`; old chunks removed from `app_providers.g.dart`.

## Test plan

- [x] `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — clean
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/settings/` — 40 passed
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/settings_screen_audio_sharing_test.dart` — 1 passed

## Next batches

After this validates the pattern, sequenced batches (per the #4506 survey):
2. Nostr Apps · 3. Permissions/Geo/Gallery · 4. Notifications · 5. Relay & Connection · 6. Content Moderation · 7. Auth & Identity · 8. Video & Feed · 9. Upload/Media + remainder

title: fix(infinite-feed): resolve issue on ios that loading-indicator always showed up
body:
Closes #4519

## Description

On iOS the infinite video feed kept showing the loading indicator after videos had loaded because `firstFrameRendered` was set `true` too early — before the Flutter texture actually contained a frame.

**Root cause:** `safePreroll` in `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.swift` marked the first frame as rendered as soon as the preroll callback fired, without verifying that the texture was actually filled. On iOS the display-link pipeline delivers the first frame with a slight delay, so Flutter briefly rendered the texture's empty (black) initial state while `firstFrameRendered` was already `true`, keeping the loading indicator visible indefinitely.

**Fix:**
- Added `tryPullFrameNow(at:)` to `VideoTextureOutput`: synchronously pulls a `CVPixelBuffer` right after preroll and pushes it into the Flutter texture, firing `onFirstFrame` on success.
- `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.safePreroll` now uses this synchronous pull; `firstFrameRendered` is only set `true` when a real buffer was delivered.
- `ControllerSubscriptions` exposes `subscribeToFirstFrame(...)` on the Dart side so the feed hides the loading indicator only after the first real frame.

title: task: extract NostrIdentity type from AuthService signing logic
body:
## Description

`AuthService` is 3400+ lines handling auth state, signer coordination, key storage, OAuth flows, multi-account registry, and profile discovery. The signing logic is scattered across multiple methods that each make independent assumptions about which key to use:

- `rpcSigner` getter (signer priority chain)
- `createAndSignEvent` (fallback to local key storage)
- `_setupUserSession` (conditional signer clearing)
- `signInForAccount` (identity restoration without PRIMARY slot sync)
- `signOut` (stale key detection per auth source)

Bug #2233 happened because two of these methods disagreed on which key to use.

### Current problems

**PRIMARY key slot as hidden shared state.** `SecureKeyStorage` has a `nostr_primary_key` slot that `withPrivateKey` always reads from, plus per-identity `saved_identity_<npub>` slots for multi-account. `switchToIdentity` copies between them, but not all code paths call it. Bug #2233 was `signInForAccount` restoring `_currentKeyContainer` from an identity slot without syncing PRIMARY.

**Public-key-only containers in identity storage.** When a keycast-only account is stored via `storeIdentityKeyContainer`, it saves a container with no private key. This lives alongside real nsecs in the same storage system. If the app falls back to local signing (e.g. keycast session expired), it loads this empty container as `_currentKeyContainer` but `withPrivateKey` reads a completely different nsec from PRIMARY, causing a pubkey/nsec mismatch.

**Keycast accounts don't need local key slots.** A pure keycast account (where the nsec lives only on the server) has no reason to store anything in local key storage. The current code stores a public-key-only container just to remember the npub, but this creates confusion between "has a key" and "has a pubkey reference."

**Local signing optimization.** When a user registers a keycast account by importing their local nsec, the same key exists both locally and on the server. The app always signs via RPC when `_keycastSigner` is set, even when it could sign locally with the same key (faster, no network round-trip). `NostrIdentity` could detect this and prefer local signing transparently.

### Proposal

Extract a `NostrIdentity` type that represents the current user's signing capability. Callers ask it to sign, it handles the how:

- Local nsec, keycast RPC, bunker, or amber, transparent to callers
- When keycast is active and the local nsec matches the same npub, prefer local signing for performance (invisible optimization)
- Keycast-only accounts hold an RPC signer reference, no local key slot
- Account switching means replacing the `NostrIdentity` instance atomically, not patching multiple fields and storage slots independently
- Eliminates the PRIMARY slot as hidden shared state

### Scope

Refactor of the signing subsystem within `AuthService`, not a full auth rewrite. `AuthService` still owns auth state, OAuth flows, and multi-account management. `NostrIdentity` owns "sign as the current user."

title: Remove Future.delayed calls in app code (22 files)
body:
**Problem**

22 files use `Future.delayed` in providers and screens where project rules discourage it in favor of proper async coordination.

**Evidence**

22 files in `mobile/lib/` use `Future.delayed` in providers and screens. Project rules (CLAUDE.md, referencing AGENTS.md) explicitly state: "Avoid introducing arbitrary `Future.delayed()` calls in app code; prefer explicit async coordination." Common uses include waiting for animations to complete, debouncing user input, and timing workarounds where proper async coordination (streams, completers, `BlocListener`) should be used instead.

**Done well**

`scroll_pagination_mixin.dart` uses Future-based coordination to prevent duplicate requests. `main.dart` uses `WidgetsBinding.addPostFrameCallback` for post-frame work. `BlocListener` with `listenWhen` is used throughout for state-driven side effects.

**Impact**

Medium. `Future.delayed` is often a symptom of a deeper issue rather than the problem itself. Developers commonly reach for an arbitrary delay as a workaround when they encounter race conditions, missing state synchronization, or lifecycle timing issues they can't fully explain — "waiting a bit" makes the problem go away without understanding why. This means each instance is a potential indicator of an underlying coordination bug: a race condition that happens to lose on slower devices, a widget reading state before it's ready, or an async gap that hasn't been properly bridged. Addressing these goes beyond code quality — replacing each delay with explicit async coordination (streams, completers, `BlocListener`, `addPostFrameCallback`) forces the actual timing contract to be understood and expressed in code, resulting in genuinely more stable behavior across devices rather than code that coincidentally works on fast hardware.

**Effort**

Low. Each occurrence needs case-by-case evaluation and replacement with proper async coordination: streams for data flow, completers for one-shot async, `BlocListener` for state-driven side effects, or `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` for post-frame work.

**Source**: [Code Review — Code Quality](docs/code-review/issues-code-quality.md)

**Problem**

\`analysis_options.yaml\` disables type-safety rules (\`invalid_assignment\`, \`return_of_invalid_type\`) and resource-leak rules (\`cancel_subscriptions\`, \`unawaited_futures\`).

**Evidence**

The app-level \`analysis_options.yaml\` disables 21 analyzer errors and 17 linter rules from \`very_good_analysis\`. Notable suppressions include: \`invalid_assignment: ignore\` and \`return_of_invalid_type: ignore\` (analyzer *errors*, not style preferences, which masks real type bugs), \`avoid_catches_without_on_clauses: ignore\`, \`unawaited_futures: ignore\`, \`avoid_dynamic_calls: false\`, \`cancel_subscriptions: false\`, \`only_throw_errors: ignore\`, \`depend_on_referenced_packages: false\`, \`implementation_imports: false\`.

**Done well**

The project adopted \`very_good_analysis\` and 33 per-package workflows enforce it. The base commitment is right; the suppressions are the gap.

**Impact**

High. Type-safety rules mask real bugs at compile time; \`cancel_subscriptions\` hides memory leaks; \`unawaited_futures\` hides fire-and-forget async with no error handling.

**Effort**

Medium. Phased re-enablement required. Start with type-safety rules as these likely indicate real bugs. Each rule re-enablement may surface existing violations that need fixing.

## Summary

Creation/editing/publishing work is currently fragmented across clip editing, transforms, camera capabilities, audio/voiceover, and publish/edit flow polish. This should be coordinated under one parent issue.

This issue is the source of truth for active video editor and creation-flow work.

## Problem

Current problems include:
- many editor-related feature asks with overlapping UX surface
- weak coordination between recording, editing, and publish flow improvements
- creation-flow polish arriving as disconnected requests instead of a sequenced area

## Scope

- clip editing
- video transforms and adjustment tools
- camera/editor capability improvements
- publish/edit flow consistency
- editor UX and polish improvements

## Candidate Related Work

- `#4185`
- `#3884`
- `#2050`
- `#1923`
- `#1512`
- `#1734`
- `#1607`
- `#2241`

Potential future mapping:
- post-merge follow-ups from current edit/publish redesign work
- additional editor/audio/overlay asks that fit this flow

## Acceptance Criteria

- creation/editor backlog is grouped under a coherent parent issue
- overlapping editor asks can be sequenced more intentionally
- future editor work has a clear coordination home

## Done When

- editor/creation work is easier to prioritize as one product area
- the biggest editor improvements are decomposed into concrete child issues

---

`@hm21`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. core editor capability gaps
2. publish/edit flow consistency
3. residual creation-flow polish

## Subgroup
- `@hm21` — DRI
- `@Chardot` — UX/design alignment
- `@realmeylisdev` — editor/state support

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a product or UX decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this issue as the coordination source of truth for editor/creation work
- distinguish core creation-flow work from unrelated feed/profile issues
- avoid spawning separate top-level issues for every editor affordance unless they are truly independent initiatives

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

title: techdebt(async): remove remaining production Future.delayed call sites

labels.name: simplicity
labels.description: Duplication, oversized files, and unnecessary complexity

body:
Source audit context: `origin/main` at commit `1be7b7790` (2026-05-18). Filed as a child of #4339 per the [ratification thread](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375). Supersedes closed-incomplete #3582.

## Severity
Medium

## Problem
`Future.delayed` is used in production app code for UI-timing coordination and ad-hoc retry/backoff. Closed issue #3582 ("Remove Future.delayed calls in app code (22 files)") was closed without the work landing — multiple production call sites remain. CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids `Future.delayed` for UI timing (use `AnimatedSwitcher`, `AnimationController`, stream listeners instead).

This issue supersedes #3582 with the scope corrected per the [#4339 ratification](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375): scoped to remaining *production* call sites only (helper docs / comments excluded). Live inventory in this issue's body, updated as call sites land.

## Evidence
- Current count: 30 `Future.delayed` call sites across 18 production files in `mobile/lib/` (excluding generated/l10n).
- Forbidden by `.claude/rules/code_style.md`: "No `Future.delayed()` for UI timing."
- Forbidden by Nostr async rules in `CLAUDE.md`: "Avoid introducing arbitrary `Future.delayed()` calls in app code; prefer explicit async coordination."
- Closed predecessor: #3582 (closed-as-completed but work not landed).
- Existing leaf already tracked: #3604 (`Cancel orphaned Future.delayed in VideoFeedItem`) — keep open as a concrete first slice; this issue tracks the broader cleanup.

## Impact
Low-Medium. Each `Future.delayed` site is an arbitrary timing assumption that breaks under jank, throttling, or test `fakeAsync`. Cumulative effect: flaky tests, brittle UI timing, orphaned futures outliving disposed widgets.

## Recommended fix
For each call site, pick one of:
1. UI timing: replace with `AnimatedSwitcher` / `AnimationController` / `TickerProvider`.
2. Retry/backoff: extract to a typed retry policy class (e.g. `ExponentialBackoff`) with cancellation support.
3. Stream coalescing: replace with a proper `StreamTransformer` (debounce / throttle / buffer).

Land per-file, not as a megafile rewrite. Each PR removes one or a small group of related call sites and adds a regression test asserting the timing-free behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `grep -rln "Future\.delayed" mobile/lib --include="*.dart" | grep -v l10n/generated | wc -l` returns 0.
- [ ] Each removed call site has a behavioral test (not a sleep-based test) that asserts the new coordination works.
- [ ] CI introduces a guard (lint or grep-based check) preventing reintroduction.

## Related
- Parent epic: #4339
- Supersedes closed-incomplete: #3582
- Concrete first slice: #3604 (VideoFeedItem-specific case)

Medium. Feed-feature engineers serialize on this file; every gesture or overlay change touches the same module. Extracting per-concern files lowers conflict and makes individual concerns testable.

## Recommended fix

- `pooled_fullscreen_item.dart`, `pooled_fullscreen_item_content.dart`, `web_fullscreen_item.dart`
- Extract gesture handling into a dedicated controller class.
- Extract analytics emission into a dedicated emitter helper.
- Keep `pooled_fullscreen_video_feed_screen.dart` as the screen-level composition only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Top-level screen file is under 600 lines.
- [ ] Each extracted widget file is under 500 lines.
- [ ] Existing repo-swap test (`pooled_video_feed_item_repo_swap_test.dart`) still passes.
- [ ] No regression in fullscreen-feed widget golden tests.

## Related

- See `state_management.md` for the `BlocProvider`-keyed-on-identity pattern this file uses — preserve it during the split.

title: refactor(providers): split app_providers.dart by feature domain

labels.name: simplicity

body:
Source audit context: `origin/main` at commit `1be7b7790` (2026-05-18). This issue extends the [April 2026 simplicity audit](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/docs/code-review/issues-simplicity.md) and is filed as a child of #4339 per the [ratification thread](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375).

## Severity
High

## Problem
`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart` has grown to 2,918 lines and is the #1 merge-conflict hotspot in the repo (114 commits over the last 90 days). It mixes Nostr-key providers, blocklist providers, curated-list state, video-feed wiring, signing adapters, performance adapters, and bridge adapters in a single file with eight section dividers but no boundary enforcement. Adding any new provider — in any domain — forces every contributor to touch the same file, and any non-trivial change ripples conflicts across in-flight feature PRs.

This is distinct from #3336, which addresses the *semantics* of `app_providers` polling. This issue addresses the *structure* — splitting the file itself.

## Evidence
- `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`: 2,918 lines, 114 commits in the last 90 days (top file by churn).
- Section dividers at lines 473, 993, 1232, 2472, 2553, 2595, 2658 — already domain-grouped in comments, but co-located in one file.
- `BlocklistVersion` class at line 1139, `CuratedListsState` at line 2211, `_AuthServiceBridgeAdapter` at line 2843, `_BlossomAuthAdapter` at line 2876, `_FirebasePerformanceAdapter` at line 2902 — different concerns, same file.
- April 2026 audit baseline: 2,500 lines. Growth: +418 lines (+17%) since the audit.

## Impact
High. Merge-conflict hotspot at #1 by 90-day commit count. The single-file structure forces serialized provider work; any independent feature touching providers stalls behind whatever else is in flight. The eight existing section dividers prove the boundaries already exist conceptually — they just need to become file boundaries.

## Recommended fix
Split by domain into `mobile/lib/providers/`:
- `auth_providers.dart` (Nostr keys, signing adapters)
- `blocklist_providers.dart` (`BlocklistVersion`, blocklist state)
- `curated_lists_providers.dart` (`CuratedListsState`, related)
- `video_providers.dart` (feed/video wiring not already extracted)
- `infrastructure_providers.dart` (Blossom, Firebase performance, bridge adapters)
- `app_providers.dart` becomes a thin re-export barrel during migration

Land one extraction PR per domain, each under ~24h, to keep conflict load on in-flight feature PRs bounded. Migrate behind a re-export barrel so consumer imports don't break across in-flight branches.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart` is under 400 lines (re-export barrel only).
- [ ] Each domain provider file is under 800 lines.
- [ ] No provider in a domain file depends on Flutter widgets directly (use repository/service abstractions).
- [ ] Each extraction PR is independently shippable and reverts cleanly.
- [ ] Riverpod codegen still passes; `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` produces no diff after the split.

## Related issues
- Parent epic: #4339
- Distinct from #3336 (DI readiness semantics — does not address file size)
- Co-sequenced with Wave 2; #3339 (state-mgmt boundaries) should land in lockstep to set the target Riverpod/BLoC division per the [ratification thread](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375).
